by Hallie Rich Jun 23, 2026 | Filed in News · OverDrive announced leadership transition with founder and CEO Steve Potash named Chairman of the Board. Marc DeBevoise will become next OverDrive CEO. As OverDrive marks its 40th year in business, founder Steve Potash is embarking on a significant leadership transition, moving from his long-held role as CEO to become the Chairman of the Board.

In preparing for his transition, Potash emphasized the need for company leadership to truly understand the transformative power of libraries. "OverDrive is never the star—the hero is the librarian," says Potash.

By shifting his focus to advocacy, partnerships, and philanthropic investment, Potash intends to expand OverDrive's impact in key global markets while personally leading the charge for a more literate and enlightened world.

results.title: OverDrive Founder Steve Potash Steps Back; Marc DeBevoise Takes Over as CEO
results.description: OverDrive founder Steve Potash (l) and newly appointed CEO Marc DeBevoise.
extra_snippets: It's the end of an era at leading library vendor OverDrive. On June 23, the company announced that the company's founder and visionary Steve Potash has stepped back from his role as CEO, handing the reins to Marc DeBevoise, who joined the company roughly four months ago as President.

"OverDrive has extraordinary reach, incredible momentum, and an enduring mission—and I’m thrilled to lead this company forward," DeBevoise said. "I'm grateful to Steve for his continued partnership and to the Board for their confidence, and I look forward to working with our team and partners to build on everything this company stands for." The move comes just days ahead of the 2026 American Library Association Annual Conference, set to run from June 25-30 in Chicago, and as the library ebook market has entered a contentious new period, with several states and municipalities considering—and three so far passing—legislation designed to rein in what librarians say are unsustainable prices and license terms from the major publishers.

Among the headlines this week: the 2026 ALA Annual Conference kicks off next week; More response to the Authors Guild's take on digital library lending; a federal judge rebukes Trump's bid to censor signage at national parks; and Arkansans speak out against potential new library restrictions.
